description: Sabotages for win-volume-sys. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: A lock that succeeds is not tried, so FSCTL_LOCK_VOLUME and FSCTL_UNLOCK_VOLUME swapped for one another are not caught: a successful lock would hold a real volume against its users, and needs an administrator. The tests show only that each control reaches the device with no buffer and returns its own error. A volume on more than one disk is not available on a development machine, so the answer that needs a second call is had from a stand-in device (extents_via), not from a real one. The device-control helper's pending path is run through its seam, overlapped_call, with an overlapped ReadFile on a named pipe, because no file-system control pends on demand; the one call that makes it a control, the DeviceIoControl argument list, is pinned by the controls themselves, and FSCTL_REQUEST_OPLOCK, which takes input and pends until another handle writes, reaches DeviceIoControl through the pending path as well. The OVERLAPPED the control is made with is a declared blind spot (see its survives entry): a control made without one answers the same on every handle tried, FSCTL_REQUEST_OPLOCK included. The abort when the wait for a pending call fails is not reachable: the event is the helper's own. The failure of CreateEventW is not reachable either.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: the extents control sends a different code
sabotages.why: The function's whole meaning is the control code it sends; a neighbouring code is refused by a volume.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: the first answer may have room for no extent
sabotages.why: The device refuses a buffer with no room for one extent (measured: ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER), so a function that asks with none fails every volume.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: a count of nothing in a more-data reply allocates a buffer with no room for an extent
sabotages.why: A reply that says it needs more room and counts none must not shrink the next buffer below the one extent the device requires.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: the retry is not bounded by its constant
sabotages.why: A loop that runs one more than the bound would spin on a volume whose extents keep changing and ask more often than the constant says.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: a refusal by the device is retried as though it needed more room
sabotages.why: Any code but ERROR_MORE_DATA ends the attempts and is the device's own; retrying it would hide it behind a report that the extents kept changing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: a call that says it wrote more than the buffer held is read
sabotages.why: A byte count beyond the buffer is the call's claim and not a fact; it is refused and not read as though the buffer held that many bytes.

sabotages.name: WV-2.2: a negative length is accepted as zero
sabotages.why: A length below zero is not a length; reporting it as an empty run would hide a damaged answer behind a plausible one.

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: an extent's offset is read from where its length is
sabotages.why: The extents are what a flush domain is found from; reading the wrong field puts every run in the wrong place. The tests build the answer from the layout Windows fixes, not from the offsets the parser uses.
find: let start = i64_at(buffer, at + offset_of!(DISK_EXTENT, StartingOffset));
replace: let start = i64_at(buffer, at + offset_of!(DISK_EXTENT, ExtentLength));

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: an answer exactly as long as its extents is refused
sabotages.why: The usual answer is exactly the size of what it counts; a bound that is off by one refuses it.

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: a negative offset is read as a very large one
sabotages.why: A device that reports a negative offset is broken, and an answer is refused rather than passed on as a run starting past the end of any disk.

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: ERROR_MORE_DATA is not recognised
sabotages.why: A volume with more extents than the first answer holds, a spanned or striped one, would then fail where it should be asked again at the size it needs.

sabotages.name: WV-1.1: an answer is asked for only once
sabotages.why: The second call, at the size the device reported, is what a volume on several disks needs.

sabotages.name: WV-1.2: a sector size of zero is accepted
sabotages.why: Zero is no sector size, and a geometry that says it means the answer is damaged; passed on, it would become an alignment that no power of two satisfies.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: the control is made without the OVERLAPPED it waits on
sabotages.why: A declared blind spot, measured and not assumed: on an overlapped handle a call with no OVERLAPPED is undefined, but the controls the tests reach take it without incident. That includes FSCTL_REQUEST_OPLOCK, the one control that pends: with no OVERLAPPED it blocks inside DeviceIoControl until the oplock breaks and answers the same, so no test can tell the two apart. The OVERLAPPED is there for the handle this crate is lent and cannot inspect.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: the event handed to an overlapped control does not suppress the completion packet
sabotages.why: A handle on a completion port gets a packet when an overlapped call completes unless the event's low bit is set. Without it a control would reach a consumer's loop as a completion it never asked for.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a control is told its output buffer is empty
sabotages.why: The buffer length the device is given is the buffer's own; a shorter one makes every control fail for want of room.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a control's input is not passed to the device
sabotages.why: An oplock request is refused without its input structure, so a helper that drops the input fails the control that takes one; none of the no-input controls could tell.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a control that completed reports no bytes written
sabotages.why: The byte count is what a caller checks the reply's size by; a count of nothing would read as an empty reply.
replace:
if started != FALSE {
        return Ok(written - written);

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a failure that is not pending is not returned
sabotages.why: Every failure but ERROR_IO_PENDING is the call's answer; treating the pending code as one reports a call that is still running as a failure while the device writes into a buffer about to be freed.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: the wait for a call still running does not wait
sabotages.why: The result is read without waiting, so a call that has not completed is reported as ERROR_IO_INCOMPLETE and the device is left writing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a call that completed after pending reports no bytes written
sabotages.why: The count a call that completed asynchronously wrote is read from GetOverlappedResult, and it is what a caller checks a reply's size by.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a call that failed after pending is reported as a success
sabotages.why: A call that pends and then fails reports its own code through GetOverlappedResult; discarding it would report success with whatever count was left.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a failure's code is clamped to what an i32 holds
sabotages.why: A code of 2^31 or more, such as the virtdisk errors, must reach the caller as the code it is; clamping or masking it names a different error. This is the defect win-error-codes exists to remove.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a failure is reported without its code
sabotages.why: The error is the device's own code, so a caller can read it with Win32Error::from_io; an error that carries none is not.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a buffer longer than a u32 counts is truncated and not refused
sabotages.why: A length that does not fit is refused, since passing its low bits would tell the device a different size from the buffer's own.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a buffer the machine cannot supply is reported under another code
sabotages.why: The size is the device's to name, so a buffer for it may not be allocatable; that is ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY, the code a caller reads as 'ask for less'.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a reply buffer is not zeroed
sabotages.why: A reply is read only as far as the device wrote, and what it did not write must be zero and not whatever the allocation held.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: a u32 is read two bytes wide
sabotages.why: A u32 is four bytes; a read two bytes wide fails to convert and every field is absent.

sabotages.name: WV-2.1: control, the end of a u32 read is saturated and not checked
sabotages.why: A control: where the end would overflow, the start is past the buffer anyway and get returns None, so saturating changes the file and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: the NUMA control sends a different code
sabotages.why: Declared blind spot. Only a volume that answers tells the control code apart from a wrong one, since a wrong code and a volume with no answer are both a refusal; the machine measured answers (node 0), but a test that required it would fail on one that does not, so none does.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: the NUMA control is told its output buffer is empty
sabotages.why: The call is made with exactly the room the structure needs; with none, a device refuses for want of room whether or not it has an answer.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: a reply larger than the structure is read as the node
sabotages.why: A reply of any size but the structure's is refused and not read, because a value taken from a buffer the device did not fill would read as a node.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: a reply smaller than the structure is read as the node
sabotages.why: The other half of the size check: a short reply leaves the buffer's remainder as it was, and reading it would report a node the device never named.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: the node is read from the first byte alone
sabotages.why: The node is a whole ULONG, carried unaltered; a value above 255 would be truncated.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: a reply that is not the structure is some other kind of error
sabotages.why: A malformed reply is InvalidData, as for every other answer in this crate that does not hold what it says; a caller tells it from a device's refusal by the kind.

sabotages.name: WV-2.3: control, the size check written as two comparisons
sabotages.why: A control: not-equal is less-or-greater, so the file changes and no behaviour. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
